1000139.etyen:
Derived from Medieval Latin Geōrgia, itself from Classical Persian گرج (“Georgian”). The exact route by which the international Latin name entered Norwegian is uncertain. The Latin form was influenced by Geōrgius (“George”), reflecting the country’s association with Saint George, but the country name is not derived from the saint's name.
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk Georgia, Italian Georgia, Portuguese Geórgia, Spanish Georgia and Romanian Georgia (“Georgia, country”).

1005003.etyen:
PIE word
 *h₂m̥bʰi
Inherited from Old Norse ambátt (“female slave, bondwoman”), from Proto-Germanic *ambahtō (“female servant”), the feminine counterpart of *ambahtaz (“servant”). The Germanic word was borrowed from Transalpine Gaulish ambaxtos (“vassal, high-ranking servant”), from Proto-Celtic *ambaxtos (“servant”), formed from *ambi- (“around”) and a derivative of *ageti (“to drive”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂m̥bʰi (“around”) and *h₂eǵ- (“to drive”).
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk ambått, Icelandic ambátt, Old Swedish ambot, Old Danish ambot, Old English ambiht and Middle English a
